feature_under_test: real Chrome execution while a separately authenticated Artifact provider process is killed and recovered

environment.mysql: ephemeral MySQL 8.4 with separate non-root migration and runtime accounts

fault_cut.provider_state_before_cut: reachable and proven by a written probe Resource
fault_cut.browser_state_before_cut: Attempt running, no Artifact persisted, and controlled origin accepted exactly one document request
fault_cut.cut: SIGKILL the separate File provider while the real Chrome document response is still in flight

invariants: the execution daemon and Artifact provider are different authenticated devices and OS processes
the provider is killed only after the Browser Attempt is running and real Chrome has started the document request
the expired Attempt produces no accepted Artifact or BackfillOutput and releases its Permit
the originating dispatch is durably settled and attempt_recovered creates a fresh dispatch identity
the recovered provider receives a distinct Attempt's DOM response and effect trace before the BackfillOutput is accepted
the DOM hash and Browser effect attestation are verified from Resource bytes
after Atoll Server restart the Executor and provider reconnect and both DOM and trace Resources remain readable

implementation.recovery_mechanism: existing Attempt TTL, persisted source dispatch fence, attempt_recovered dispatch, and idempotent Artifact/result contracts

non_claims: remote cloud or object-storage provider behavior
simultaneous SIGKILL of both Chrome and the Artifact provider
third-party JavaScript, authentication, anti-bot or availability behavior
Browser throughput or long-window production SLO

acceptance.gate: P9 real Chrome execution combined with separate local File provider process outage
